title: Workday Jobs Scraper & API - Paste Any Careers URL

careersUrls.title: Workday careers URLs
careersUrls.description: Any URL from the company's Workday careers site - the careers home, a search page, or a single job posting. All three unguessable parts (tenant, wd-shard, site name) are read out of the URL. A compact tenant/wd5/SiteName triple also works.

searchText.title: Search text
searchText.description: Passed to Workday's own server-side search - the same box on the careers page. Narrows results before they are fetched, so you are billed only for what matches.

titleKeywords.title: Title keywords
titleKeywords.description: Keep only jobs whose title contains any of these.

excludeKeywords.title: Exclude keywords
excludeKeywords.description: Drop jobs whose title matches any of these.

locations.title: Locations
locations.description: Keep only jobs whose location matches any of these.

remoteOnly.title: Remote only
remoteOnly.description: Keep only jobs whose location reads as remote.

postedWithinDays.title: Posted within (days)
postedWithinDays.description: 0 = no limit. Uses the date derived from Workday's posted-on text (pinned to en-US). Past 30 days Workday only says '30+ Days Ago', so windows above 30 cannot exclude older postings - turn on includeDescription to use each job's real start date instead.

includeDescription.title: Include full description
includeDescription.description: Fetches each job's detail record: full HTML description, employment type and the real posting date. One extra request per job, so a 2,000-role tenant takes noticeably longer.

outputMode.title: What each row should be
outputMode.description: "jobs" is one row per opening, "companies" is one row per board, "both" is the job rows followed by the summaries.

onlyNewSinceLastRun.title: Only what changed since the last run
onlyNewSinceLastRun.description: Return only jobs that opened since your last run (isNew) and jobs that have since closed (isClosed). The first run records a baseline and returns everything. Built for a daily schedule: a run with no changes returns nothing and costs only the start fee. Changing the URLs or filters starts a fresh baseline.

maxJobsPerBoard.title: Max jobs per board
maxJobsPerBoard.description: Cap results per board. 0 means no limit. Starts at 10 so a first trial run stays cheap - clear it to get everything.

concurrency.title: Concurrency
concurrency.description: Boards fetched in parallel. The endpoint pages at 20 jobs per request, so large tenants take many requests either way - this bounds politeness, not speed.
